A stalled client loop must not create unbounded memory growth or silent command loss.

Completion event

Game-loop command drain
Game objects and script runtime state are not socket-thread safe.

MCP adapter boundary
Transport compatibility must not falsely standardize one game's QA surface.

Project-owned listener
The current protocol is reusable, but listener policy and shipping risk remain project responsibilities.

Version project observations
Last Frontier and TLA legitimately expose different game models.
The observation object carries a project-owned schema version and enough readiness/action metadata for its adapter; the Engine protocol does not define game fields.
The project client loop, not the socket thread, owns game state mutation.

entries.source: The envelope is versioned but experimental; embedding projects must pin an Engine revision and own their observation and action schemas.
Disabled by default
A control listener is a security-sensitive development feature.
An embedding project must require explicit configuration to start a listener.
Loopback first
The protocol has no transport encryption or peer identity beyond a shared token.
Listeners and clients default to 127.0.0.1 and refuse non-loopback operation without explicit operator opt-in.
No TLS
Token authentication is not confidentiality or replay protection.
Treat the shared token and all payloads as plaintext on the TCP path; use an authenticated encrypted tunnel if non-loopback transport is unavoidable.
Remote token required
An empty-token remote listener is an unauthenticated process-control channel.
A sample or project listener exposed beyond loopback requires a non-empty token in addition to explicit remote opt-in.
Environment-backed token
Command lines, process listings, shell history, and reports are common secret leak paths.
Reference tools read tokens from a named environment variable and do not accept or print raw token arguments.
Preserve server authority
AI QA should exercise the same validation boundary as a player.
Project actions use normal client input or authenticated gameplay RPC paths; the bridge does not grant server authority or administrator capability by default.
Compile out shipping surface
Removing the socket and command path reduces attack and antivirus heuristic surface.
Projects should compile the listener and remote-command path out of production clients, not merely disable them in a runtime config.
Normal gameplay path
A successful protocol smoke cannot prove game authorization or anti-cheat boundaries.
Project tests show representative actions pass through ordinary server validation and that rejected gameplay actions complete as failures.
Malformed peer responses
Automation must fail closed instead of consuming ambiguous data.
Client tests reject malformed JSON, unsupported envelopes, mismatched ids, dual result/error responses, and oversized lines.
Project native integration
The Python sample is protocol proof, not FOnline native runtime proof.
A real project separately builds its native bridge, starts an actual client, verifies queue draining on the client loop, and checks clean shutdown/reconnect behavior.
Protocol smoke
A rendered schema alone cannot prove connection state and asynchronous lifecycle behavior.
Run the reference client against the sample server and prove auth, liveness, status, observation, invalid input, action acceptance, completion, state update, and event cursor behavior.
Security boundary tests
Security prose must remain executable as the helper evolves.
Tests prove non-loopback refusal, per-connection authorization, wrong-token rejection, and absence of token command-line arguments.
Shipping artifact inspection
A disabled default is weaker than absence from the shipped binary.
Release validation confirms production clients cannot open the AiControl listener and do not contain the project remote-command implementation.
Bounded line size
A local automation channel still needs deterministic memory bounds.
A request or response JSON payload is at most 1 MiB before the LF terminator; oversized input is rejected and the connection may close.
One JSON object per line
Line framing is streamable, inspectable, and shared by both audited project bridges.
Each request and response is one JSON object terminated by LF; peers process lines in connection order.
Request envelope
A small JSON-RPC-shaped envelope gives correlation without claiming the full JSON-RPC specification.
A request object carries jsonrpc=2.0, a caller-chosen id, a non-empty method string, and an object-valued params member.
Response envelope
Strict correlation prevents one automation step from consuming another step's result.
A response echoes jsonrpc=2.0 and the request id, then contains exactly one of result or error; error contains an integer code and string message.
Sequential request processing
The contract remains implementable by a single project-owned listener and avoids hidden ordering races.
A client sends a request and consumes its matching response before reusing that connection; clients must not require multiplexing or concurrent in-flight requests.
TCP byte stream
The common project implementations are local tooling channels, not an internet service protocol.
A bridge accepts an explicitly configured TCP endpoint; clients must not assume service discovery, TLS, HTTP, or WebSocket framing.
UTF-8 encoding
Project observations and action payloads may contain localized text.
JSON lines are encoded and decoded as strict UTF-8; malformed input receives a parse error or closes the connection.

ACM playback shape
These values are assigned by playback role after CACMUnpacker runs.
Expect ACM effects to decode as mono and ACM music as stereo signed 16-bit samples at 22050 Hz.
Audio callback mixing
The SDL stream callback asks SoundManager to fill output while game-thread play/stop operations can add or erase sounds.
Treat playback as client audio-callback work; mutations of the active sound list must hold the audio-device lock.
Device conversion
SoundManager does not require authored assets to match one fixed hardware format.
Let AppAudio convert decoded sample format, channel count, and rate to the active SDL output-device format before playback.
Ogg streaming
SoundManager uses a platform-sized streaming portion and clears OggStream when the first read reaches EOF.
Expect Ogg Vorbis to decode in 64 KiB native chunks and 128 KiB Web chunks; short files are retained fully and release the stream after the initial decode.
Unsupported extension limitation
This is a documented implementation limitation, not support for arbitrary audio formats; callers and content validation must keep unsupported suffixes out.
Author only wav, acm, or ogg paths. The current loader has no fallback rejection branch, so another explicit suffix bypasses all decoders and can enqueue an empty sound while returning success.
WAV chunk order
The loader is a focused sequential reader, not a general RIFF chunk walker.
Place RIFF, WAVE, fmt, optional fact, and data in the exact order expected by LoadWav.
WAV PCM widths
LoadWav maps only those two widths to AppAudio formats before device conversion.
Author WAV as uncompressed PCM with either 8-bit unsigned or 16-bit signed samples; channel count and sample rate may vary and are converted by the frontend.
Client sound index
Game.PlaySound resolves through the prebuilt name map rather than scanning the filesystem on each call.
Call ResourceManager.IndexFiles after client resources are available; it indexes every wav, acm, and ogg path for effect-name lookup.
Effect identity
PlaySound erases the caller suffix and lowercases the name before querying ResourceManager's identically normalized index.
Treat an effect identity as the lowercase resource path with its final extension removed.
Duplicate-stem precedence
ResourceManager uses map::emplace while iterating the fixed extension array, so later formats do not replace an existing stem.
Do not ship multiple wav/acm/ogg resources with the same normalized effect stem; when they collide, the first indexed extension wins in wav, acm, ogg order.
Music path ownership
PlayMusic forwards the supplied filename directly to SoundManager.Load.
Pass music as an exact resource path; unlike effects, music is not resolved through the normalized sound-name index.
Raw-copy delivery
There is no dedicated audio baker; runtime decoders require the original bytes and relative path.
Keep acm, ogg, and wav in Baking.RawCopyFileExtensions and include RawCopy in every resource pack that owns runtime audio.
Source-backed contract for FOnline audio resource delivery, decoding, playback, mixing, script entry points, and validation boundaries.
Legacy Fallout ACM
ACM compatibility exists for classic Fallout assets, but its playback shape is fixed by SoundManager instead of inferred from a modern container.
Supply an Interplay ACM stream accepted by CACMUnpacker; the stock playback contract treats effects as mono and music as stereo signed 16-bit audio at 22050 Hz.
Legacy effects and music decoded fully before playback
Ogg Vorbis
The implementation uses libvorbisfile callbacks over the engine FileSystem and does not provide a generic Ogg-codec dispatch layer.
Use an Ogg bitstream containing Vorbis audio; SoundManager decodes signed 16-bit interleaved data and retains the decoder only when more than the first chunk remains.
Modern effects or streaming music
PCM WAV
The stock loader is deliberately narrower than the general WAV family and rejects compression, unsupported sample widths, and unexpected chunk order.
Use a RIFF/WAVE file with an immediate fmt chunk, optional fact chunk, an immediate data chunk, PCM format tag 1, and 8-bit unsigned or 16-bit signed samples.
Short effects or music decoded fully before playback
Missing extension fallback
The default extension belongs to SoundManager.Load, while PlaySound normalizes before Load.
An exact music path without an extension receives .acm; effect lookup ignores the caller extension and resolves by indexed stem.
Disabled audio return convention
Inactive playback and zero effect volume intentionally return success without loading a resource.
Do not use a true PlaySound or PlayMusic result as resource-existence proof when audio is disabled, unavailable, or effect volume is zero.
Game.PlaySound
The script method delegates to SoundManager.PlaySound with the indexed resource-name map.
Use Game.PlaySound on the client for non-music playback and inspect its bool result when audio is active and SoundVolume is nonzero.
Base effect before variants
Variant discovery runs only after the base lookup misses.
If the normalized base effect exists, play it directly and do not select numbered alternatives.
Contiguous numbered variants
SoundManager counts consecutive map hits and chooses uniformly from 1 through count.
To randomize an absent base effect, provide a contiguous one-based sequence NAME_1 through NAME_N; discovery stops at the first missing suffix.
No stock spatial source
The stock playback object has no world position, radius, pan, or per-instance volume field.
Treat every SoundManager sound as a global client mix input; implement listener selection, distance policy, or recipient filtering in project code.
Game.PlayMusic
The script entry point owns the empty-name stop convention before delegating to SoundManager.
Use Game.PlayMusic with an exact resource path and repeat interval; an empty path stops current music and succeeds.
Repeat interval
ProcessSound schedules NextPlayTime using a one-millisecond threshold and rewinds retained Ogg streams before replay.
Pass a nonzero repeatTime to replay after completion; values at or below one millisecond repeat immediately, and larger values insert that delay.
Sound and music volumes
SoundManager selects a volume by IsMusic and AppAudio normalizes the clamped percentage before SDL mixing.
Control effects with Audio.SoundVolume and music with Audio.MusicVolume; the frontend clamps each mix operation to 0 through 100.
Single music stream
SoundManager.PlayMusic calls StopMusic before Load, so a failed replacement does not restore the previous track.
Expect a new music request to stop every existing music instance before attempting to load the replacement.

entries.source: The three current decoders and client playback behavior are revision-pinned while focused native decoder fixtures and a versioned compatibility policy are still missing.
Decoder diagnostics
The loaders report format-specific failure boundaries instead of substituting silence as a valid resource.

Treat false playback results and RIFF, PCM, ACM, Ogg, or conversion log lines as authoring failures; reject unsupported suffixes in content validation because the runtime currently has no diagnostic for them.
Source-backed reference
The generated model rejects extension, decoder, chunk-size, default, setting, and headless drift before prose can silently become stale.
Regenerate and check the audio model whenever SoundManager, ResourceManager, AppAudio, settings, raw-copy delivery, or script entry points change.
Headless boundary
Headless audio deliberately exposes no active device or callback.
Do not claim audible validation from a headless or stub application; AppAudio is disabled there and playback may report no-op success.
Focused native test gap
RawCopyBaker and broad client tests do not execute the codec and callback contract documented here.
Keep the absence of focused SoundManager decoder/playback fixtures visible until tests cover valid and invalid WAV, ACM, Ogg, variant, repeat, and replacement behavior.
Embedding-project ownership
The engine supplies decoding and a global client mixer, not a complete game audio design or asset-governance system.
Keep catalog conventions, spatial/recipient policy, mastering, licenses, attribution, budgets, and gameplay triggers in project documentation and tests.
Baking gate
Documentation checks can prove configured extension coverage but cannot prove an embedding project's resource-pack wiring.
Bake a pack containing representative audio and verify the expected relative paths and original bytes reach client resources.
Visible audible validation
Only an active platform audio device can prove conversion, callback scheduling, mixing, and audible output.
On every claimed platform, use a visible client with audio enabled to play one asset per format, a numbered effect family, a replacement track, delayed and immediate repeats, and volume endpoints.

Generated shader prelude
Authored shaders share one compile-time shape contract and must not duplicate these directives.
The baker prepends '#version <Version> es', 'precision highp float', MAX_SCRIPT_VALUES, and, in 3D builds, MAX_BONES and MAX_TEXTURES before ShaderCommon and stage text.
glslang target environment
All backend flavors derive from the same validated linked program.
Both stages compile as GLSL for a Vulkan 1.0 client and SPIR-V 1.0 target, then link and build reflection once per pass.
Incremental output set
A missing or stale flavor must make the effect eligible for rebaking.
The bake checker tracks the source copy, pass metadata, and every stage/flavor artifact for every declared pass.
Stage interface validation
Location/type mismatches and syntax errors fail the resource bake before runtime.
Vertex and fragment stages must parse, link, and expose a valid reflection model for every pass.
Per-pass metadata
Runtime backends consume reflection results without running glslang.
Each pass emits an info artifact with [EffectInfo] native bindings and [EffectInfoSdl] per-stage dense slots and resource counts.
Native and cross-compiled flavors
One source effect supports the active renderer backends without project-side shader forks.
Each stage emits native Vulkan SPIR-V, desktop GLSL 330, GLSL ES 300, HLSL Shader Model 4.0, and Metal source for macOS and iOS.
SDL_GPU descriptor remap
Native Vulkan bindings remain untouched while SDL_GPU gets dense stage-local slots.
The baker copies native SPIR-V, rewrites descriptor sets and bindings to SDL_GPU's per-stage convention, and emits the result as spv_sdl. Metal source is compiled from the remapped module.
Baked source copy
RenderEffect reparses [Effect] state at runtime; the source file is part of the runtime artifact set.
The original .fofx source is written to the baked resource set after all pass artifacts.
Number of WorldMatrices entries exposed to 3D effects through ModelBuf and the MAX_BONES shader define.

Number of float slots in ScriptValueBuf. The value must be positive and divisible by four because the GLSL declaration is an array of vec4 values and the native buffer is 16-byte aligned.
Source-backed authoring, baking, renderer-resource, runtime-loading, and script-control contract for FOnline .fofx effects.
Unknown tokens fail effect construction instead of falling back silently.
The value selects one accepted blend equation. A pass-specific key inherits the unsuffixed default when absent.
The runtime parses factors before each backend creates its blend state.
The value contains exactly two accepted tokens: source factor followed by destination factor. A pass-specific key inherits the unsuffixed default when absent.
Models and particle emitter nodes can carry independent culling intent, while backend pipeline/state multiplication remains opt-in.
Enable this only when callers need to select None, Back, or Front face culling per draw. Without it, the effect accepts only the default None mode.
Depth-dependent effects must choose comparison explicitly because the default never rejects a fragment.
The value selects one accepted depth comparison. A pass-specific key inherits the unsuffixed default when absent.
Particle emitter nodes carry depth intent independently from their shader, while ordinary effects should not pay for unused backend objects and pipelines.

Enable this only when callers need to select depth-test and depth-write state per draw. The renderer then builds all four test/write combinations; otherwise only the state declared by DepthWrite and DepthFunc exists.

UI, primitive, and flush targets may have no depth attachment even though the state remains present in the effect; variant-aware backends resolve the selected slot instead of reading the default directly.

The value is parsed as a boolean and provides the default depth-write state for QuadSprite and Model usages when the active target has a depth attachment. A draw may select another state only when DepthVariants is enabled.
State overrides and stage overrides use intentionally different config spellings.
BlendFunc, BlendEquation, DepthWrite, and DepthFunc support an exact one-based _PassN suffix. Shader sections use a space before PassN instead.
The runtime allocates fixed per-pass arrays and validates the authored count before loading metadata.
Passes must be in the inclusive range 1..EFFECT_MAX_PASSES. Pass indices in section names and state suffixes are one-based.
Shadow execution can be disabled independently at runtime for 3D draws.
ShadowPass is -1 for no shadow pass or a one-based pass index in 1..EFFECT_MAX_PASSES. It marks that pass as the model shadow pass.
The authored source omits its own version directive because the baker supplies it.
Version is parsed as an integer and emitted as '#version <Version> es' for glslang input.
CameraBuf affine bases
The scale terms preserve continuity across padded/chunked render targets and zoom.
CameraBuf contains MapAnchorScreenPos and ChunkScreenAnchor. Shaders evaluate either basis as '.xy + TexCoord * .zw' for world-anchored or screen-anchored coordinates.
Explicit bindings
SDL_GPU slot assignment sorts authored bindings and remaps them to dense per-stage slots.
Every live sampler and uniform block must declare an explicit binding. Binding numbers must be unique within each shader stage and resource class.
General uniform buffers
EffectBaker validates reflected byte sizes against RenderEffect buffer structures.

Recognized general buffers are ProjBuf, MainTexBuf, EggBuf, SpriteBorderBuf, ParticleSamplingBuf, TimeBuf, RandomValueBuf, ScriptValueBuf, and CameraBuf. ParticleSamplingBuf is caller-defined per draw for particle texture sampling and distortion controls. Declarations must match the native std140-compatible layouts exactly.
3D uniform buffers
These layouts carry skinning, lighting, texture-atlas, and animation timing data for model effects.
Recognized model buffers are ModelBuf, ModelTexBuf, and ModelAnimBuf, with MAX_BONES and MAX_TEXTURES supplied by the baker prelude.
Native Vulkan descriptor convention
The native SPIR-V is consumed unchanged by Rendering-Vulkan and is the source for GLSL, GLSL ES, and HLSL cross-compilation.
Author native shader resources with uniform buffers in descriptor set 0 and combined image samplers in descriptor set 1.
Renderer-provided samplers
A shader may compile with another sampler name but receives no Engine-owned texture binding.

The runtime has producers for MainTex, IndoorMaskTex, and BackgroundTex, plus ModelTex0 through ModelTexN-1 in 3D builds. BackgroundTex is a caller-supplied scene snapshot for refraction. Other reflected sampler names are not populated by RenderEffect.
ScriptValueBuf
The baker supplies MAX_SCRIPT_VALUES and the client API writes float ranges into the same native buffer.
Declare 'vec4 ScriptValue[MAX_SCRIPT_VALUES / 4]' inside ScriptValueBuf. The flat script-facing index range is 0..EFFECT_SCRIPT_VALUES-1.
SDL_GPU per-stage limits
SDL_CreateGPUShader requires per-stage counts and the backend descriptor convention differs from native Vulkan.
Each shader stage may use at most 16 samplers and 4 uniform buffers. Slots become dense independently for vertex samplers, vertex UBOs, fragment samplers, and fragment UBOs.
Per-frame buffers
These buffers are updated per loaded effect only when reflection reports that the effect needs them.
TimeBuf exposes FrameTime.x and GameTime.x as session-relative seconds wrapped at 8192; RandomValueBuf exposes four independent [0,1] values refreshed each frame.
Unsupported shader resources
The renderer binds only its fixed buffer vocabulary and sampled textures.
Unknown uniform blocks, storage buffers, and storage images are rejected. Dead declared descriptor resources are rejected during SDL SPIR-V patching.
Vertex2D input layout
The non-model usages share one native vertex structure even when a shader ignores some inputs.
ImGui, QuadSprite, and Primitive effects consume locations 0..3 from Vertex2D: vec3 position, normalized color, vec2 texture coordinate, and vec2 egg/auxiliary data.
Vertex3D input layout
All model shaders must match the fixed Vertex3D layout configured by every active backend.
Model effects consume locations 0..8: position, normal, primary UV, base UV, tangent, bitangent, blend weights, blend indices, and color.
Path-only effect cache
ScriptValueBuf and per-frame optional buffers belong to the cached object, not to an effect slot.
EffectManager caches one mutable RenderEffect object per resource path. Re-loading the same path returns the existing object.
Default effect resolution
Projects can temporarily override a slot and restore the Engine/project default without naming its path.
An empty SetEffect path resolves back to the slot's default effect; a non-empty path loads it using the default effect's EffectUsage.
First-load EffectUsage
The cache key omits EffectUsage and later loads return the first object without rebuilding its vertex layout or pipeline assumptions.
The first load of a path fixes that RenderEffect object's EffectUsage. Do not reuse one path across incompatible ImGui, QuadSprite, Primitive, or Model usage categories.
Per-frame buffer updates
Declaring a built-in buffer opts the effect into its Engine producer.
Every loaded effect is visited each frame; TimeBuf and RandomValueBuf are allocated/refreshed only when reflection marks them as needed.
ScriptValue persistence
Switching to another path selects another object's buffer, while switching back to a previously loaded path restores that object's prior values.
An effect declaring ScriptValueBuf receives a zeroed buffer on first load. Values persist on the cached path until overwritten or explicitly cleared; SetEffect does not clear them.
Script-value target resolution
Writing a slot on a passthrough/default effect without ScriptValueBuf is a script error.
Script writes resolve the currently selected effect for one EffectType/subtype, require it to be loaded, and require that it declares ScriptValueBuf.
Runtime artifact pair
Changing only a shader binary cannot change pass count or blend/depth state.
RenderEffect loads the baked .fofx source for pass/render state and one .fofx-N-info artifact per pass for reflected resource positions.

Writes one float into the selected cached effect object's ScriptValueBuf.
Single-value writes suit infrequent scalar tuning.
The index must be in range and the selected effect must be loaded and declare ScriptValueBuf.
Writes a contiguous slice of values in one native call; valuesCount -1 selects the remaining input range.
Bulk writes avoid repeated native calls for parameter blocks updated together.
Input offset/count and destination range are validated before resolving and writing the effect.
[Effect]
Both the baker and runtime loader reject a source without this section.
Every .fofx source must contain an Effect section. It stores pass count, shader version, shadow-pass selection, and default or per-pass render state.
[FragmentShader] and [FragmentShader PassN]
Multi-pass effects often share geometry processing and vary only the fragment stage.
Each declared pass needs non-empty fragment shader text. The baker first reads FragmentShader PassN and falls back to the generic FragmentShader section when the pass-specific section is empty.
[ShaderCommon]
It is the only format-level reuse block; the .fofx parser has no include directive.
ShaderCommon is optional raw shader text prepended to both stages of every pass after the Engine-generated prelude.
[VertexShader] and [VertexShader PassN]
A shared vertex stage can serve all passes while selected passes override it.
Each declared pass needs non-empty vertex shader text. The baker first reads VertexShader PassN and falls back to the generic VertexShader section when the pass-specific section is empty.
Descriptor bindings
Dense SDL slot remapping must be deterministic and complete.
Reject missing explicit bindings, duplicate same-stage bindings, dead descriptor declarations, and SDL_GPU stage-limit overflow.
Uniform buffer layout
All backends upload fixed native structures without per-shader layout adaptation.
Reject known uniform buffers whose reflected byte size differs from the corresponding RenderEffect structure and reject every unknown uniform block.
Compiler diagnostics
Build logs remain machine-readable while preserving the shader compiler message.
Shader parse/link/reflection failures stop effect baking and normalize compiler diagnostics to a single log line.
Cross-backend visible validation
Cross-compilation cannot prove driver behavior, feature-level support, visual output, or performance.
Validate project effects on every renderer/backend profile the embedding project ships, including depth/blend-sensitive scenes and the lowest supported shader profile.
Reflection metadata
Backends depend on metadata identity even when shader compilation itself succeeds.
Verify native [EffectInfo] binding values and SDL [EffectInfoSdl] counts/slots for representative effects.
Baked flavor completeness
A resource can pass one backend and still be incomplete for another package.
Verify source, metadata, native SPIR-V, SDL SPIR-V, GLSL, GLSL ES, HLSL, and both MSL outputs for every stage/pass.
Project contract validation
The Engine can validate format mechanics but cannot infer project shader semantics or art-direction intent.
An embedding project must validate every effect path, EffectType/subtype assignment, ScriptValue slot registry, buffer writer, resource-pack override, and visible fallback it owns.
Required source content
A partial source cannot produce a complete linked program or runtime state.
Reject a missing Effect section or a pass without usable vertex or fragment text.
Bind-time downscale
Binding area-averages glyph pixels and rounds metrics once; values above one and nonpositive or nonfinite values are rejected.
Pass a finite defaultScale in (0, 1]; use a larger authored bitmap and downscale it rather than requesting runtime upscaling.
Exact extension dispatch
Dispatch uses case-sensitive ends_with checks and does not sniff descriptor content.
Call Game.BindFont with an exact lowercase .fofnt or .fnt path; every other suffix throws a script exception.
Project-extensible font slots
FontType is an indexed loaded-font table, and unloaded or out-of-range slots throw.
Bind every FontType slot before it is measured or drawn; the Engine names only Default = 0 and embedding scripts may extend the enum through codegen annotations.
Interface sprite atlas
Both Game.BindFont descriptor branches pass the same interface atlas type.
Script-bound fonts allocate their normal and optional bordered textures in AtlasType::IfaceSprites.
Separately baked image
The descriptor is raw-copied, but its image is loaded through SpriteManager and the normal image-format pipeline.
Ship the referenced image as an independently supported image resource in the same pack and preserve its relative path.
Descriptor raw-copy boundary
There is no dedicated font descriptor baker; RawCopyBaker preserves path and bytes.
Keep fofnt and fnt in Baking.RawCopyFileExtensions so descriptor bytes reach baked resources unchanged.
Slot replacement and cache reset
StoreFont replaces the optional table entry, rebuilds atlas data, and clears the format cache.
Treat a repeated binding of the same slot as replacement; all cached layouts are discarded before the rebuilt font is used.
Updater fallback font
Updater binds the Default slot from that exact path with skip-if-loaded behavior.
Keep Fonts/Default.fofnt available for the built-in updater path unless the host replaces that resource contract deliberately.
Binary v3 signature
Any other signature or BMFont version is rejected before block parsing.
The first four bytes must be B, M, F, and binary-format version 3.
Fixed block order
The parser advances by each block size and reads the next block payload directly; it does not search by block type.
Export Info, Common, Pages, and Chars blocks in standard binary order without interposed optional blocks.
Twenty-byte character records
Bundled fonts contain negative bearings, so this source-backed limitation must remain visible instead of being documented as correct signed decoding.

Encode each Chars record in the 20-byte BMFont v3 layout. The format defines signed xoffset, yoffset, and xadvance fields, but the current loader reads all three as unsigned little-endian uint16 values; avoid negative metrics until that runtime defect is fixed separately.
Grayscale and border preparation
This makes runtime tinting and FontFlag::Bordered available without descriptor-specific switches.
Binary BMFont bindings always normalize nontransparent pixels to gray and create a second bordered atlas copy.
One-pixel exporter padding
The loader requires the four padding bytes to equal 0x01010101 and later removes one pixel from each side of every glyph rectangle.
Set BMFont Info padding up, right, down, and left to exactly one pixel each.
Derived line metrics
The BMFont Common.lineHeight field is used for bearing conversion but is not copied directly into the Engine line height.
Expect Engine LineHeight to use the visible W glyph height when W exists, otherwise Common.base; YAdvance is half that resulting height.
Engine metric conversion
The Engine samples an expanded rectangle for antialiasing and optional border dilation while keeping the visible glyph metrics separate.
Reserve one transparent pixel around every glyph; the loader shifts x/y inward, removes two pixels from width/height, negates bearings, and adds one pixel to xadvance.
Relative page image
The Pages payload is read as one string and combined with the descriptor directory before sprite loading.
Store a NUL-terminated page filename resolvable relative to the .fnt descriptor directory.
Single texture page
The Common block page count must be one; multi-page BMFont descriptors are rejected.
Export exactly one texture page.
Source-backed contract for FOnline FOFNT and binary BMFont descriptors, client font binding, text layout, rendering, scaling, caching, and validation.
End and comments
End stops parsing, while the parser strips comment markers from the current key token rather than implementing a line-oriented comment grammar.
Terminate the useful descriptor with End; # and ; begin comments only when encountered inside the whitespace-delimited key token.
Height
Rendering samples Height plus two pixels and the maximum height can define an omitted LineHeight.
Set the visible glyph rectangle height, excluding the one-pixel sampling border.
Image

The current loader accesses image_name.back() without an empty guard, so authoring validation must enforce this mandatory field before runtime; the trailing marker is removed before relative resource resolution.
Name a non-empty image resource relative to the descriptor; append * to request grayscale normalization and runtime tinting.
Letter
The parser decodes exactly one codepoint to select the glyph map entry; later duplicate records overwrite earlier metrics.
Start each glyph record with Letter and one valid UTF-8 codepoint after the first apostrophe.
LineHeight
BuildFont replaces zero LineHeight with the maximum glyph height after optional scaling.
Set the glyph-line height in pixels, or leave it zero/omitted to derive the maximum authored glyph height.
OffsetX
The descriptor value is stored unchanged and subtracted when generating glyph vertices.
Set the signed horizontal bearing in Engine coordinates; drawing places the quad at cursor X minus OffsetX.
OffsetY
The descriptor value is stored unchanged and subtracted when generating glyph vertices.
Set the signed vertical bearing in Engine coordinates; drawing places the quad at cursor Y minus OffsetY.
PositionX
BuildFont converts this position, expanded by one padding pixel, into texture coordinates.
Set the glyph rectangle's left coordinate in the image.
PositionY
BuildFont converts this position, expanded by one padding pixel, into texture coordinates.
Set the glyph rectangle's top coordinate in the image.
Version
The parser requires the first key to be Version and uses 2 as its current maximum accepted version.
Make Version the first parsed key; author version 2 for current resources. Values greater than 2 are rejected.
Width
Rendering samples Width plus two pixels and bind-time scaling rewrites the visible size.
Set the visible glyph rectangle width, excluding the one-pixel sampling border.
XAdvance
The glyph advance drives wrapping and drawing, and the space glyph's XAdvance becomes SpaceWidth.
Set the horizontal cursor advance after the glyph; include an explicit space glyph when spaces must consume width.
YAdvance
Layout advances by LineHeight plus YAdvance and scales the value at bind time.
Set the extra vertical gap added between consecutive text lines.
The default raw-copy list contains bmfc, but the runtime extension dispatch contains only fofnt and fnt.
Treat .bmfc as an optional BMFont tool configuration file and never pass it to Game.BindFont.
Raw-copied authoring sidecar; not a runtime descriptor
The client reads the binary BMF header and fixed block layout; text and XML BMFont files are not accepted.
Export BMFont binary version 3 with one texture page and one-pixel padding on every side of each glyph.
Runtime descriptor
Game.BindFont dispatches the exact lowercase .fofnt suffix to FontManager::BindFoFont.
Use the Engine text descriptor when authoring explicit image, line, and per-codepoint glyph metrics.
Runtime descriptor
Horizontal alignment
The initial and every post-newline X coordinate are recalculated from that line's measured width.
CenterX and AlignRight position each line independently inside the supplied rectangle; do not combine contradictory alignment flags.
Justification
Tabs are fixed at four SpaceWidth units and are not justification opportunities.
Justify distributes remaining finite rectangle width over breakable spaces on wrapped non-skipped lines.
Measurement matches layout
Measurement and drawing share GetOrFormat, skips, line metrics, and bind-time scale; NoWrap truncation is intentionally gated to Draw mode.
Use Game.GetTextInfo and related line helpers with the same rectangle and TextFormat used for drawing, but do not infer draw-only NoWrap truncation from measurement.
NoWrap and TruncateLine
These flags intentionally choose different loss behavior and should not be treated as synonyms.
NoWrap ends draw text at the first width overflow; TruncateLine removes overflowing glyphs through the next authored newline.
SkipLines and KeepTail
These mechanisms serve pagination and log-tail behavior but use different counters and overflow conditions.
SkipLines removes leading lines by default and trailing lines with AlignBottom; KeepTail discards leading overflow so the newest visible lines remain.
TextFormat value
The exported value type is a fixed 12-byte layout consumed by measurement and drawing.
Pass a Font slot, FontFlag bitmask, and nonnegative SkipLines count as TextFormat.
UTF-8 and missing glyphs
The layout maps invalid sequences to codepoint zero and unknown codepoints to zero advance, while drawing skips missing map entries.
Author every required Unicode codepoint; invalid UTF-8 and absent glyphs consume no glyph width and render no fallback symbol.
Vertical alignment
Vertical placement depends on the number of lines that fit, not the total source-string byte length.
CenterY centers the visible block and AlignBottom places it against the rectangle bottom using LineHeight and YAdvance.
Width overflow and wrapping
Layout mutates its cached text copy to establish line boundaries without changing the caller's source string.
With finite width, default layout wraps at the latest space or tab and inserts a line break before an overlong token when no break point exists.
Vertically align the text block to the rect's bottom edge; also flips TextFormat::SkipLines from "skip from top" to "skip from bottom"
Right-align each line within the rect
Render glyphs from the bordered/outlined font texture variant instead of the regular one
Horizontally center each line within the rect
Vertically center the text block within the rect
Justify each line: distribute extra spaces between words to fill the rect width
When the text block is taller than the rect, render its tail (skip the leading overflowing lines)
Strip inline color tags (@color:0x...@ / @color@), but render text with the base color as-is
On rect-width overflow truncate the rest of the text instead of wrapping it to the next line
No additional behavior

No additional behavior
Area-average downsampling
The scaler uses alpha-weighted area averages, clears the original glyph rectangle, and keeps the same top-left position.
Expect defaultScale below one to rewrite the bound atlas region and integer glyph metrics once, with no per-widget font scale.
Bordered atlas copy
The loader duplicates the image and fills transparent neighbors of visible pixels before calculating bordered UVs.
Reserve transparent padding for a one-pixel black dilation; FontFlag::Bordered selects the generated second texture.
Shared and per-slot font effect
Draw batching keys include the selected texture and RenderEffect pointer.
Fonts start with the Engine shared font effect; a per-slot EffectType::Font override replaces it and a null override returns to the shared effect.
Grayscale normalization and tint
Nontransparent RGB becomes 128/128/128 while alpha is preserved; transparent pixels are cleared.
Use a trailing * on FOFNT Image, or binary BMFont, when the bitmap should be normalized to middle gray and tinted by draw color.
Inline color tags
Formatting removes valid markers before wrapping and records color transitions by output byte offset.
Use @color:BBGGRR@ or @color:AABBGGRR@, optionally with a 0x prefix, to push a color and @color@ to restore the previous color; NoColorize strips valid tags without applying them.
Three-frame layout cache
The cache is a client implementation detail and is cleared whenever fonts are stored or cleared.
Do not depend on cached layout identity or lifetime; the cache key includes text, font, flags, skips, rectangle size, color, and mode and expires after three unused frames.
One-pixel sampling border
Texture coordinates and submitted quads expand each visible glyph by one pixel on all sides.
Leave at least one pixel of valid transparent padding around every glyph rectangle and around the image edge.

BMFont header, padding, and pages
The runtime has explicit exceptions for all three incompatibilities.
Reject BMFont descriptors that are not binary v3, do not use 1/1/1/1 padding, or declare any page count other than one.
Descriptor and image presence
Pre-runtime validation must cover the omitted-Image case because the loader reaches image_name.back() before it can produce a diagnostic.

Fail the asset gate when the descriptor is missing, FOFNT omits Image, or the relative image cannot load as an atlas sprite. The runtime reports missing descriptor and image files, but currently has no explicit empty-Image guard.
Embedding-project bake and visible check
A raw-copy success cannot prove glyph coverage, atlas padding, typography, backend rendering, or GUI fit.
Bake descriptor and image resources, run measurement tests for every bound scale, and visibly inspect regular, bordered, wrapped, aligned, localized, and missing-glyph cases.
Engine regression gates
Structural checks pin source-derived contracts while native tests cover resource and client construction paths.
Run the focused documentation test and the full generated Engine unit-test target after FontManager or font descriptor changes.
FOFNT header and UTF-8
These are hard parser failures rather than recoverable missing-glyph cases.
Reject a FOFNT whose first key is not Version, whose version exceeds 2, or whose Letter line does not contain one valid UTF-8 codepoint.
Generated contract drift
The checked model makes silent source/documentation drift fail CI.
Regenerate and check the font-format model whenever parser keys, binary constants, font enums, binding dispatch, raw-copy defaults, scale, cache, or bundled descriptors change.
Scale range
The Engine supports deterministic bind-time downscaling, not bitmap upscaling.
Reject NaN, infinity, zero, negative values, and values greater than one before mutating the font table or atlas.
Unsigned BMFont metric limitation
Values such as -2 are currently reinterpreted as 65534 and can move rendered glyphs far outside their intended position; the runtime fix belongs in a separate code change.
Track that the current loader reads xoffset, yoffset, and xadvance with GetLEUInt16 even though bundled binary fonts contain negative bearings.

Source-backed contract for the reusable FOnline AngelScript GUI object model, screen stack, layout, rendering, input dispatch, project hooks, and validation boundaries.
Active-screen hit order
Screen stack and tree order jointly define hit priority.
Mouse input starts at the top active screen; children are tested from last to first so later children are visually and interactively above earlier siblings.
Drag and drop
The runtime owns gesture and dispatch mechanics while projects own transfer semantics.
Start dragging from a draggable pressed object, draw it in the cursor pass, and evaluate registered drop handlers in order until one returns true.
Input event subscriptions
Projects should not duplicate the same forwarding subscriptions.
Include Input.fos once; its ModuleInit subscribes mouse, key, and input-loss Game events and forwards them to Gui engine callbacks.
Keyboard dispatch order
Global shortcuts, command entry, and focused controls have distinct precedence.
Dispatch global input to active screens from top to bottom, then the active console, then focused objects when the console is absent or inactive.
Per-frame hit-test cache
Cursor drawing, zoom, and movement repeat the same query in one frame, while FindHit walks every active screen tree.

Cache CheckHit for one Game.FrameTime and query position; invalidate it whenever active state, persistent geometry, screen order, scroll, crop, transparent-hit images, or hittability can change the result.
Input-loss reset
Alt-tab and window-focus changes must not leave sticky input or drag state.
On focus/input loss, release tracked keys and mouse buttons, unhover and unfocus objects, cancel a pressed object as lost, and notify the drop menu.
Modal and close-on-miss behavior
Modal screens block fallthrough while nonmodal windows can be reordered by interaction.
Close a close-on-miss screen on an unhandled left click; only a nonmodal screen may search lower active screens for a hit and bring one forward.
Pressed-object repeat
Controls that use OnMousePressed depend on these fixed timings.
After mouse down, begin repeated pressed callbacks after 500 ms and continue every 40 ms while the pointer still hits the pressed object.
Client hook bridge
The runtime implements these hooks but does not subscribe project render/lifecycle events for itself.
Call EngineCallback_Start, EngineCallback_Loop, EngineCallback_Draw, and optionally EngineCallback_DrawCursor from the embedding client's corresponding events.
Font and image dependencies
The GUI runtime delegates text layout and sprite loading/drawing to the reusable font and image systems.
Bind every FontType used by Text nodes and deliver every sprite referenced by Panel or Button before showing affected screens.
No Engine declarative GUI format
Declarative sources and generators belong to embedding projects or a separately versioned companion tool.
Treat Gui.fos and Input.fos as an AngelScript runtime API; do not claim that Engine parses .fogui, .foguischeme, or another layout format.
Project enum extension
Engine supplies reusable baseline values while each game owns its screen and cursor catalog.
Extend GuiScreen and CursorType through project metadata without redefining the Engine sentinels.
Script render scope
Native ClientEngine enables script drawing around OnRenderIface and processes video before ending the scene.
Draw GUI only from the client OnRenderIface scope where script drawing is enabled; place the cursor pass at the project-selected top layer.
Touch adaptation boundary
ClientEngine emits separate touch events while the reusable Input module subscribes only mouse, key, and input-loss events.
Do not assume Input.fos routes native touch events into GUI mouse callbacks; provide and validate project/platform adaptation when touch interaction is required.
Anchor and centering
Unanchored controls remain centered when a parent or viewport changes size.
Anchor selected axes to parent edges; center an axis with no matching edge bit by half the live-size minus authored-base-size delta.
Crop affects drawing and hit testing
Visual clipping and interaction clipping must agree.
When Panel crop is enabled, scissor descendant drawing and reject hit tests outside the panel rectangle.
Dock precedence
Dock and Anchor are alternative layout modes rather than cumulative constraints.
When Dock is not None, use the selected Left, Right, Top, Bottom, or Fill rule and ignore Anchor positioning.
9-slice frame
Frame images can resize without distorting corners or producing invalid UV ranges.
Use SetFrameImage plus nonnegative cap insets measured in source pixels; the runtime clamps source and destination caps and stretches edges and center.
Grid prototype cloning
The prototype remains hidden while clones become the live repeated content.
Point Grid at a named object prototype, choose a positive column count, and let ResizeGrid clone, index, initialize, and position the cells.
Parent coordinate space
The same layout algorithm serves nested widgets and viewport-level screens.
Interpret authored positions and sizes relative to the parent; root objects use Settings.View.ScreenWidth and ScreenHeight as the live parent size.
Panel scrolling
Scroll values are stateful layout offsets rather than a renderer-only transform.
Enable vertical and/or horizontal auto-scroll explicitly; target changes animate for PanelScrollAnimationDurationMs and drawing refreshes active tweens.
Cursor screen ownership
The cursor is excluded from the ordinary screen stack and ordinary screen draw pass.
Register GuiScreen::Cursor as the dedicated always-active CursorScreen and draw it explicitly through EngineCallback_DrawCursor.
Explicit resolution and language refresh
The reusable runtime does not subscribe these project lifecycle transitions itself.
Call Callback_OnResolutionChanged after viewport changes and Callback_OnLanguageChanged after language changes.
Project screen initializer
The reusable runtime owns screen mechanics but intentionally does not own a game screen catalog.
Provide namespace GuiScreens with void InitializeScreens(); EngineCallback_Start calls it and cannot compile or start without that project contract.
Registration and precache
Registration is executable client startup work, not passive metadata loading.
Register each non-None GuiScreen id with a factory; registration replaces the old entry and constructs one screen immediately for initialization and resource precache.
Show and hide callback order
Project callbacks often distinguish data refresh from top-of-stack visibility.
Treat Show as active-state setup, OnShow traversal, then OnAppear traversal; treat Hide as OnDisappear, OnHide traversal, inactive state, event fire, and optional multiinstance removal.
Single and multiinstance ownership
The flag changes construction, persistence, lookup, and teardown semantics.
Reuse a registered single-instance screen; create a fresh screen for each multiinstance show and remove that instance after hide.

entries.source: Helper command lines are revision-pinned implementation interfaces; automation must pin an engine revision.
Private container header
The shared SpriteResource decoder validates the versioned framing before any client or tool consumes pixels or mesh data.
The private baked stream starts with SpriteResource magic 43 and version 2, then uint16 frame count, uint16 whole animation ticks, and uint8 direction count, and ends with magic 43.
Direction records
Per-frame offsets preserve screen placement when polygon geometry changes the serialized canvas independently for each direction and animation frame.
Each of one or GameSettings::MAP_DIR_COUNT directions stores exactly the common frame count; the resolved logical root offset is serialized on every concrete frame after mesh padding and cropping.
Scan and targeted modes
Incremental project builds and one-file rebakes share one baker without treating a skipped target as failure.
An empty target scans every registered extension; a targeted missing, unsupported, or BakeChecker-skipped path returns without output.
Per-file work and aggregate failure
A full scan reports all independently failing image resources in one run without silently succeeding.
Selected files bake asynchronously; each exception is logged, and any nonzero error count ends the Image baker with ImageBakerException.
Case-insensitive extension dispatch
Mixed-case extensions resolve to the same registered loader, though projects should still use canonical lowercase paths.
Source and runtime extension lookup uses get_file_extension(), which returns the extension without its dot and lowercases it.
Concrete and shared frame records
The record preserves logical placement and lighting coordinates while avoiding transparent texture rows and submitting indexed silhouettes; repeated frames still reuse the original payload.

Each frame starts with a shared flag; a concrete record stores signed int16 draw offset, uint16 cropped dimensions, signed int16 NextX/NextY, exact RGBA8 pixels, a mesh kind, and mesh vertices and indices plus logical source size and origin when the kind is Mesh. A shared record stores one earlier-frame index.
Output path and NewName
FRM/FRx critter normalization and split-direction aggregation require deterministic renamed resources.
The baked resource normally keeps its source path; loaders may set NewName, which replaces that output path for legacy normalization.
Dollar option dispatch
One source file can produce selected or transformed variants through FOFRM references without duplicate binaries.
LoadAny strips text after '$' from the physical filename, passes that suffix to the selected loader, and resolves the source inside the same FileCollection.
Per-pack SpriteInfo index
Common EngineMetadata can answer 2D animation queries on server and client without decoding RGBA payloads; losing or introducing the aggregate index requires a full rebake.
Image baking maintains SpriteInfo/<PackName>.foinfo version 1 with duration, direction, frame bounds, offsets, and shared-frame metadata for every current image source in that resource pack.
Optional polygonal sprite mesh

The opt-in path reduces transparent overdraw and texture area without clipping visible pixels or changing gameplay placement; unsafe or unprofitable candidates remain quads and empty masks remain explicit empty geometry.

Resolve and validate the complete SpriteMesh setting group for every image bake, including when SpriteMesh.Enabled is false: AlphaThreshold is 0..254, MaxTriangles is positive, and AreaSavingsWeight is finite and non-negative. When enabled, build deterministic alpha-thresholded candidates within that triangle budget, score saved original-frame area against submitted triangles, retain only validated coverage, crop selected mesh canvases to exact geometry bounds, and preserve the logical root through the serialized frame offset.
Source-backed import, FOFRM composition, polygonal sprite meshing, baked-container, client sprite, atlas, cache, and validation contract for FOnline images.
count / Count
Each referenced source can itself contain multiple frames.
Count is the number of descriptor references per direction, defaults to one, and must be positive; it is not necessarily the final flattened frame count.
[dir_N] / [Dir_N]
SpriteSheet accepts exactly one direction or GameSettings::MAP_DIR_COUNT directions.
A descriptor is either single-direction or supplies every Engine map direction; partial direction sets and later gaps fail.
effect / Effect
Authors must not treat a parsed-but-unused field as a rendering contract.
The parser accepts effect/Effect into FrameCollection.EffectName for compatibility, but ImageBaker does not serialize or apply it and the stock runtime never selects an effect from this field.
Nested sequence flattening
The merge loop copies child Main frames only and validates each later direction against collection.SequenceSize.

FOFRM appends the Main sequence of every referenced child; child direction sheets and child sequence offsets are not composed, and all authored parent directions must flatten to the same final frame count.
fps / Fps
The authored count and fps determine whole-sheet AnimTicks, while runtime playback divides that duration by flattened frame count.
FOFRM reads lowercase fps first and then legacy Fps; zero creates a non-playing sheet, while production animation values must also keep whole duration per frame above zero.
next_x_N / next_y_N and NextX_N / NextY_N
This preserves source-format displacement while allowing authored composition corrections.
Descriptor frame deltas are added to every flattened child frame's imported NextX/NextY values.
frm / Frm and frm_N / Frm_N
References are joined with the descriptor directory and then dispatched by the referenced extension.
Every authored descriptor slot resolves one relative image path; only slot zero also accepts the unnumbered frm/Frm alias.
offs_x / offs_y and OffsetX / OffsetY
The parser reuses the current ox/oy variables instead of resetting them for each direction.
Sequence offsets are signed and may be authored in the root or each direction section; explicitly set both values in every direction section because omitted values carry forward.
FOFRM whole-sequence timing
Nested animated references can therefore change effective frame cadence unless the author accounts for flattening.
FOFRM computes whole-sequence duration from authored descriptor count, not from the flattened child-frame count; fps zero yields zero ticks.
Options are parsed from the source reference without changing the physical source filename.

Digits select the last requested available palette, T derives alpha from maximum RGB while index zero remains transparent, H/V mirror, and F selects an inclusive ascending or descending clamped frame/range; letters are case-insensitive and unknown characters are ignored.
The source can expose many cycles while one resource path needs deterministic output.

The integer before '-' selects a cycle and an optional non-negative integer after '-' selects one frame; out-of-range cycle/frame values fall back to zero, while no frame selector imports the whole cycle.
The importer composes palette layers and animation selection before writing runtime RGBA frames.

Zero or more bracket entries set clamped RGB offsets for part 0 other, 1 skin, 2 hair, or 3 armor; an out-of-range part applies the RGB values to all parts, and text after the last bracket selects a sequence case-insensitively (empty selects the first).
baker and default runtime
ART direction numbering and frame metadata require format-specific remapping before runtime use.
ART imports raw or RLE frames, palettes, offsets, frame rate, static or eight-rotation data, and the palette/alpha/mirror/frame filename options.
baker and default runtime
Cycle/frame lookup and palette transparency are part of the legacy format rather than generic sprite behavior.
BAM imports one selected cycle or one selected frame, supports packed BAMC input and RLE, derives frame deltas, and treats palette blue 255 as transparent.
baker and default runtime
It is the only built-in text descriptor that can combine sources, add frame deltas, and produce a runtime-loadable .fofrm path.
FOFRM composes relative image references into one static image, animation, or complete direction sheet and is the preferred authored wrapper for multi-frame or option-bearing sources.
baker and default runtime
The split legacy representation must become one runtime direction sheet with a deterministic output path.
A .fr0 entry discovers its numbered directional siblings, rejects a gap after direction loading begins, and renames baked output to lowercase .fofrm for critter paths or .frm otherwise.
baker and default runtime
The importer preserves legacy frame geometry while normalizing pixels into the Engine RGBA container.
FRM imports big-endian frame timing, offsets, deltas, one or complete direction tables, optional same-basename .pal data, and animated default-palette indices.
baker and default runtime
Packed and unpacked files share one extension and normalize to one RGBA frame.
MOS imports one tiled palette image; MOSC is decompressed first, and palette color 0x00FF00 is made transparent.
baker and default runtime
PNG is the recommended lossless authored source for ordinary project images and transparent sprites.
PNG is decoded through libpng, strips 16-bit channels to 8-bit, expands palette/low-bit grayscale/tRNS data, and fills missing alpha with 255 before emitting one RGBA frame.
baker and default runtime
The format has no authored animation or direction metadata.
RIX imports one opaque indexed image using its embedded palette and emits one RGBA frame.
baker only by default; wrap through FOFRM for the stock runtime
Directly baked .spr output cannot be loaded by the default client; a .fofrm wrapper gives the output a registered extension without changing imported pixels.
SPR imports named sequences, layered parts, direction remapping, color offsets, repeated-frame sharing, and fixed 10 fps, but the stock DefaultSpriteFactory does not register the .spr extension.
baker and default runtime
Indexed, grayscale, other bit depths, image IDs, and alternate-origin assumptions are outside the implemented production subset.
TGA supports only raw type 2 or RLE type 10 TrueColor input at 24 or 32 bpp, converts BGR(A) to RGBA, and flips rows bottom-to-top.
baker and default runtime
The loader supplies timing because the legacy container exposes a frame list rather than an Engine animation descriptor.
TIL imports its nested ZAR frames as a 10 fps single-direction sequence.
baker and default runtime
ZAR is a single-image legacy container used directly and inside TIL.
ZAR imports one palette-backed raw or RLE image with alpha into one RGBA frame.
Atlas upload, polygon draw, border, and hit mask
Mesh geometry changes fill and submission cost without changing atlas pixels, picking, logical scaling, or specialized rectangular rendering contracts.

Positive-size RGBA frames are placed in the requested AtlasType, uploaded with duplicated one-pixel filtering edges, and converted to a SpriteHitValue hit mask. Ordinary full-image draws submit the baked indexed silhouette when present; crops, tiled and padded draws, fonts, blits, model sprites, and particles retain rectangular paths.
Copyable sprite cache identity
Independent animation state must not mutate the cached prototype, and different atlas classes cannot share placement blindly.
Copyable sprites are cached by hashed path plus AtlasType and each load returns MakeCopy, so the same source path may have separate atlas-backed cache entries.
Baked-container decoding
Source decoders are baker-only and are not deployed as runtime image parsers.

The stock runtime reads only the baked container through ReadSpriteResource, validates magic, version, frame and direction counts, complete frame/mesh records, footer, and trailing data, then constructs either AtlasSprite or SpriteSheet.
Default factory extension boundary
Bake support and stock runtime path support are separate extension registries.
DefaultSpriteFactory registers every built-in ImageBaker extension except spr; direct .spr paths need a custom factory or, normally, an authored .fofrm wrapper.
Per-frame sprite offsets
Visual root-motion displacement must remain separate from sequence placement and authoritative world movement.

Concrete and shared SpriteSheet frames retain imported NextX/NextY in _sprOffset; ordinary drawing uses the selected AtlasSprite offset, while locomotion projection consumes the separate frame-offset array.
Missing-path memoization
Adding a previously missing resource during a live session normally requires recreating the manager or restarting the client before retrying the same path.
Missing paths, absent extensions, unknown factories, and factory load failures are memoized by path in _nonFoundSprites; CleanupSpriteCache does not clear that set.
Direction and playback state
Animation state is client presentation state and each direction owns a parallel frame sheet.
SpriteSheet accepts one or the full map direction count, supports direction selection, random prewarm, normalized time, loop/reverse playback, and treats one frame or zero whole ticks as non-playing.
Single-frame behavior
NextX/NextY matter only when a sheet consumer selects and interprets animation frames.

A one-frame one-direction resource becomes AtlasSprite and applies the resolved concrete-frame draw offset; serialized NextX/NextY remains metadata because there is no SpriteSheet frame-displacement surface.

A descriptor must resolve at least one source reference before a runtime frame table can exist.

No nested shared frame records

Malformed decoder inputs
Legacy binary parsers must fail deterministically instead of emitting truncated runtime containers.

Nonzero per-frame duration
SpriteSheet::Update divides elapsed time by integer ticks_per_frame, while Play only guards one frame or zero whole ticks.
For a playing multi-frame sheet, author timing so whole AnimTicks divided by flattened frame count is at least one millisecond; fps zero intentionally disables playback.

Exact RGBA payload size
The client reads a fixed RGBA8 byte count without a separate payload-length field.

entries.source: SPARK and Effekseer are independent optional backends. Embedding projects must pin an Engine revision and explicitly enable, test, and support the formats they ship.
Standalone Effekseer Editor
The editor has an isolated auxiliary build and staged payload.
Build and stage the Windows Effekseer authoring tool through buildtools.py build-auxiliary; do not ship it as a game runtime dependency.
Effekseer dependency cache
The cache invalidates an effect when its project or dependencies change.
Let ParticleBaker track compiler-reported dependency snapshots; force a full rebake after changing compiler behavior.
Backend-neutral Mapper preview
The preview uses the same ParticleSystem facade and runtime extensions as the game.
Preview baked .spk and .efk resources through the Mapper particle window using explicit placement, seed, scale, offset, and optional prewarm.
Serializer-normalized round trip
The editor saves an object graph, not a token-preserving XML syntax tree.
Expect Save to rewrite object ordering, optional/default fields, nesting, references, and formatting according to the SPARK graph serializer; review the semantic diff.
Mapper SPARK editor
The editor reads source assets while previewing the baked runtime form.
Edit raw .spark assets in Mapper, save through the SPARK XML saver, then rebake and recreate the .spk preview.
Particle baker tests
The native suite exercises both backend bake boundaries.
Run the ParticleBaker unit tests after changing source formats, transforms, path checks, compiler output, or dependency invalidation.
Documentation contract
The manifest validates every source anchor and generated page.
Run docs_particle_format.py --check and its focused unit test after changing particle formats, backends, tools, or integrations.
Effekseer runtime tests
The suite checks deterministic callback geometry and supported runtime behavior.
Run the focused Effekseer runtime tests after changing compiler/runtime geometry, sorting, batching, textures, seed, or scale.
Model attachment route
ParticleSprite tests do not exercise model-bone ownership or projection.
For AttachParticles or Critter.RunParticle changes, visibly verify the target bone, offset, active layer lifetime, animation, and FO_ENABLE_3D profile.
Embedding-project bake
Only the project bake sees its complete resource graph and feature selection.
Rebake an affected embedding project and reject authored .spk/.efk, malformed sources, missing dependencies, and stale generated resources.
Both render routes
Headless parsing cannot prove framing, alpha, blend, depth, orientation, or world-scale behavior.
Visibly check atlas particles and direct-scene particles at their real draw order, camera angle, scale, depth occluders, and supported renderer backends.
Visible runtime validation
Successful compilation cannot prove visual correctness or gameplay timing.
Inspect every affected backend and integration route in Mapper and a representative client scene, including depth, clipping, lifetime, transforms, and performance.
Semicolon arrays
convert2Array splits only on semicolons and returns false for an empty conversion result.
Separate array values with semicolons; each element is converted independently and at least one converted value is required before assignment.
Attribute elements
The loader ignores non-attrib children at attribute level and looks up each id in the descriptor.
Serialize descriptor values as attrib children with a non-empty id matching the object's descriptor attribute name.
Effekseer dependency paths
Dependency snapshots and compilation resolve against the physical project directory and reject escapes.
Keep compiler-reported dependencies relative and inside the directory resource source that owns the project.
Effekseer project XML
The native compiler rejects malformed XML and unsupported profile features during baking.
An .efkproj source must be a non-empty EffekseerProject XML document supported by the fixed compiler profile.
Names and unknown attributes
Names have a dedicated descriptor path, and typoed attributes do not affect the loaded object.
Write an object's optional display name in its name XML attribute. Unknown non-empty attrib ids are logged as warnings and skipped rather than becoming custom data.
Registered object tags
Graph::addNode fails when IOManager cannot construct the named object.
Every object element name must match one of the registered object tags in the generated catalog.
Nested objects and references
The loader resolves both inline graph nodes and integer reference IDs, while the saver emits references according to graph sharing.
Reference attributes may nest an object directly or identify a previously described shared object through ref; arrays of references use nested objects and Ref children.
SPARK document root
The XML loader rejects missing or differently named roots before graph construction.
The document element must be named SPARK exactly.
Exactly one System
Graph validation selects the sole System as the load result.
The graph must contain exactly one System object; nested helper objects do not replace it and a second System is invalid.
SPARK XML graph
Baking fails when loadFromBuffer("xml", ...) returns no system.
A .spark source must be accepted by the vendored SPARK XML loader and contain a usable System graph.
SPARK texture paths
The baker rejects absolute and escaping paths before producing .spk.
SPARK texture paths must be relative, contain no line-control characters, and remain inside the particle's resource source.
Value attribute or text
XMLLoader::getValue checks the value attribute first and otherwise reads child text.
A scalar or array value may be written in the attrib value XML attribute or as element text; value takes precedence when both exist.

ProtoBaker and ProtoTextBaker track the active parent path and reject self, pair, and longer cycles under every repeated-parent policy.
Acyclic inheritance
Prototype parent graphs must be acyclic.
Prototype files use the shared ConfigFile parser; quoted or escaped comment characters remain part of the value.
Configuration syntax
Use repeated INI-like sections, key = value assignments, # comments, whitespace-prefixed trailing backslash continuation, and key += value append where appropriate.
Directories and conventional extension names do not select a prototype type; the section does.
Extension filter
Only files whose extension occurs in Baking.ProtoFileExtensions enter ProtoBaker.
The baker rejects either character after applying the file-basename fallback and before hashing or duplicate detection.
Reserved identifier characters
Prototype ids must not contain / or $ because both characters are reserved for nested section addressing.
The same text id may exist in different prototype types; duplicate ids in one type fail the bake.
Identity and duplicates
A migration-resolved prototype id must be unique within its resolved type across the complete pack input.
$-prefixed control directives are not copied into the merged property map.
Inheritance precedence
Merge ancestors depth first, then parents from left to right, then the child; later property values replace earlier values.
Parents may be declared in another file, but cross-type and missing parents fail the bake.
Inheritance scope
Every parent must resolve inside the same prototype type and current pack input.
Server baking validates ScriptFuncType metadata for every authored callback property and rejects missing functions or mismatched signatures before runtime.
InitScript callback signatures
A non-empty built-in Item, Critter, Map, or Location InitScript property must resolve to a global void callback receiving that entity type and bool firstTime.
Unknown, disabled-for-this-side, virtual, and temporary properties are rejected; opposite-side-only properties are skipped for that side.
Property resolution
Every non-control key must resolve to a property available for the current bake side.
Author migrations in native/project metadata with ///@ MigrationRule Proto <Type> <Old> <NewOrRemove>.
Prototype migration
Proto migration rules are applied to declared ids, parent ids, lookups, and persisted references before final resolution.
A removed or renamed referenced id needs an explicit Proto migration rule to a valid target or Remove according to the owning persistence policy.
Prototype references
FixedType and Proto entity property references must resolve after migration unless the property is nullable and the authored value is empty.
The default is permissive; set the option false when a project wants every inheritance diamond to fail baking. ProtoBaker and ProtoTextBaker apply the same rule.
Repeated ancestors
A parent reached through several inheritance paths contributes only where it is first reached; Baking.AllowRepeatedProtoParents decides whether the later reach is skipped or rejected.
A source property can be meaningful on one side and skipped on another; server output also validates script callback properties.
Side-specific output
The same source set is parsed and serialized separately for server, client, and mapper metadata.
The property serializer is the authority for scalar, enum, struct, array, dictionary, RefType, FixedType, and Proto reference text.
Strict text values
Property values must parse according to the metadata type without overflow, unknown enum/prototype references, non-finite numbers, or malformed collection structure.

Source-backed authoring, baking, normalization, runtime lookup, and rendering contract for FOnline text packs and prototype-localized text.
Bake-time fallback
Runtime lookup loads already-normalized binary packs and does not perform fallback.
Missing packs and keys are copied from each language's configured fallback during baking; packs and keys absent from that fallback are removed.
Base language
TextPack::ParseBakeLanguages validates the ordered declarations before either text baker consumes them.
Baking.BakeLanguages must be non-empty and its first bare language is the default normalization base.
Baked filename
TextPack::LoadFromResources later requires exactly those three basename segments.
Raw and prototype text bakers emit <ResourcePack>.<TextPack>.<Language>.fotxt-bin.
Base source required
TextBaker cannot normalize a changed pack without the base language and throws before parsing output.
For every changed raw text pack, the selected file set must contain the base-language source.
Fallback declaration
An explicit parent forms an ordered bake-time fallback chain, while a bare non-first language falls back to the first language.
Each BakeLanguages entry is language or child:parent; names are unique and a parent must appear before its child.
Source filename
TextBaker rejects every other basename shape.
A .fotxt basename contains exactly two dot-separated segments: text-pack name and language identifier.
Language identifier
Acceptance is equality against the language names parsed from Baking.BakeLanguages; no length or locale-shape validator exists.
The Engine treats the filename suffix as an opaque configured string and imposes no fixed character count.
Incremental pack completion
A partial language update must still pass complete-pack normalization.
When one language file of a text pack changes, TextBaker includes every configured language file for that same pack in the rebake.
Unsupported language
Unsupported raw languages do not create binary packs.
A raw text file whose suffix is absent from Baking.BakeLanguages is warned and skipped.
Variant cardinality
FixStr tests only whether a key count is zero and preserves all existing variants when the key exists.
Normalization aligns key presence, not the number or ordering of duplicate variants under an existing key.
Complete output set
The binary output shape is deterministic across projects and language sets.
ProtoTextBaker creates all five generated packs for every configured language, including empty packs.
Omitted language
The same ordered base-language contract is shared with raw text packs.
When the language token is omitted, a $Text field belongs to the first Baking.BakeLanguages entry.
Escaped value decoding
Sequences such as \n become actual newline characters in the baked value.
Prototype $Text values pass through StringEscaping::DecodeString before entering the text pack.
Inherited text
A child inherits missing exact text keys while its own exact key assignment replaces the inherited value.
Parent $Text fields are merged recursively before the child fields.
Cross-type intersections
Intersections are counted as errors and abort prototype text baking.
Two prototype sources may not emit the same complete key into one generated pack and language.
Generated pack routing
These five names are the reusable Engine-generated prototype text-pack set.
Item, Critter, Map, and Location prototypes route to Items, Critters, Maps, and Locations; other non-exported HasProtos entity or fixed types route to Protos.
Prototype text key
The prototype id becomes Key1 and the optional trailing tokens become Key2 and Key3.
Prototype text uses $Text [Language] [Key2] [Key3] = Value and accepts at most four key tokens including $Text.
Unsupported prototype language
Prototype-localized text follows the configured output-language set.
A $Text language absent from Baking.BakeLanguages is warned and omitted.
Inline color tags
Color tags are renderer syntax, independent from text-pack parsing and project lexem formatting.
The client font renderer recognizes @color:HEX@ to push a six- or eight-hex-digit color and @color@ to restore the previous color.
NoColorize
The formatting pass always removes recognized tags, but writes per-glyph colors only when colorization is enabled.
FontFlag.NoColorize strips valid inline color tags while rendering all glyphs with the base color.
