entries.source: The contract is generated for a pinned Engine revision. Projects own language policy, pack catalogs, translation workflow, semantic key conventions, and any game-specific lexem or argument formatter.
No comment grammar
LoadFromString has no comment-token branch and begins parsing at the first opening brace anywhere on the line.
The parser skips a physical line only when it cannot find the first opening brace; comment conventions are project policy and comment text must not contain parseable brace fields.
Required and optional fields
The parser rejects only an empty collection or first key after all three fields were extracted.
The collection and Key1 must be non-empty; Key2 and Text may be empty.
Raw entry shape
LoadFromString supplies the collection separately and constructs TextPackKey from the two authored key fields.
A parsed .fotxt entry contains Key1, Key2, and Text in three brace-delimited fields; the collection is the text-pack filename segment.
Structured key identity
Raw .fotxt entries leave Key3 empty, while prototype $Text fields may populate Key2 and Key3.
TextPackKey identity is Collection plus Key1, Key2, and Key3, each represented as a hashed string wrapper.
Multiline value
The first two ExtractBraceToken calls disable multiline input and the third enables it.
Only the third field may continue across physical lines; joined lines retain newline characters until the first closing brace.
Closing-brace boundary
ExtractBraceToken searches directly for the next closing brace and does not decode escapes.
The first closing brace terminates each field; the raw format has no escape sequence for a literal closing brace inside Text.
Duplicate-key variants
Variant count and indexed selection are explicit runtime operations; duplicate cardinality is not language-normalized.
Multiple entries may share the same complete TextPackKey and remain ordered variants in the baked multimap.
Empty BakeLanguages
No deterministic base language can be selected.
TextBaker, ProtoTextBaker, and TextPack normalization reject an empty Baking.BakeLanguages list.
Malformed raw text
LoadFromString reports aggregate failure and TextBaker rejects the complete source file.
A raw source with a missing required field or unterminated value fails the text bake even if other entries parsed successfully.
Prototype output intersection
The generated pack must not depend on iteration order across type catalogs.
Duplicate complete keys produced by different prototype type sources in one output pack fail baking.
Prototype key token count
TextPackKey has no additional key field.
A prototype $Text key with more than Language, Key2, and Key3 after $Text fails baking.
Unsupported raw language warning
Projects can keep unrelated sources in a broader input tree without silently publishing them.
Unsupported raw language files produce a warning and no output for that language.
Decode failure stops playback
Frame errors log and call Stop; end-of-stream also stops the clip.
Treat malformed frame data, color output failure, unsupported pixel format, and end-of-stream as stop conditions and inspect client logs.
Clock-derived frame selection
RenderFrame multiplies elapsed seconds by the Theora fps ratio and decodes the positive frame difference.
Author valid fps numerator and denominator metadata; frame selection derives the target frame from elapsed monotonic time and decoder cost.
Theora header selection
Construction fails when packet seeking, setup data, or decoder allocation fails.
Provide a stream whose headers are accepted by th_decode_headerin and whose setup can allocate a decoder context.
No container-audio decode
VideoClip links Theora packet decoding only, while fullscreen pairing starts SoundManager music from the path after a vertical bar.
Do not rely on an audio stream embedded in the Ogg video; author audio as a separate client music resource when needed.
Ogg page and packet ingestion
DecodePacket owns a fixed ten-stream state table and copies bounded portions from the in-memory resource.
Treat the input as Ogg pages read into the sync layer in 1024-byte portions and support at most ten simultaneously discovered logical streams.
Supported chroma subsampling
The CPU conversion chooses chroma divisors only for those three enum values.
Use TH_PF_420, TH_PF_422, or TH_PF_444; any other Theora pixel format stops playback.
CPU RGBA output
RenderFrame writes clamped RGB components and alpha 0xFF into RenderedTextureData.
Expect each decoded frame to be converted from YCbCr to opaque RGBA on the CPU before texture upload.
Client runtime ownership
Decoding, texture creation, drawing, and exported methods live in the client layer.
Deliver video to client resources and invoke playback on the client or mapper runtime.
Exact resource path
Both fullscreen and script-owned paths call Resources.ReadFile with the supplied path.
Pass the complete delivered video path, including its extension; video lookup has no default suffix or normalized stem index.
Whole-resource memory budget
ReadFile.GetData moves the complete resource into VideoClip.RawVideoData before packet decoding.
Budget compressed file bytes, one CPU RGBA frame, and one GPU texture for each active playback; the stock path is not streaming from the resource store.
Raw-copy delivery
There is no video baker; playback consumes the delivered bytes.
Keep ogv in Baking.RawCopyFileExtensions and include RawCopy in the client-only resource pack that owns video files.
Source-backed contract for FOnline Ogg/Theora video delivery, decoding, fullscreen playback, script-owned playback, rendering, and validation boundaries.
Script-owned playback creation
The exported PassOwnership method loads the resource, constructs VideoClip, creates a texture, and stores both in VideoPlayback.
Use Game.CreateVideoPlayback(exactPath, looped) to create an independent ref-counted playback and texture.
Creation failure throws
Unlike fullscreen PlayVideo, CreateVideoPlayback converts a missing ReadFile result into ScriptException.
Catch or prevent a missing script-owned video resource; creation throws Video file not found.
Null and completed instances are no-ops
DrawVideoPlayback returns early for both states after enforcing render scope.
Passing null or an instance whose playback resources were cleared performs no draw and does not throw.
Positive target size advances
RenderFrame is called only inside the positive-size branch.
Pass a positive width and height every frame; zero or negative size skips frame decode, texture upload, and drawing.
Caller-owned rectangle and aspect
DrawVideoPlayback constructs irect32 directly from the script arguments.
Choose and maintain the target rectangle and aspect policy in project UI code; the Engine draws exactly the supplied position and size.
RenderIface-only drawing
The method throws outside the client script draw scope.
Call Game.DrawVideoPlayback only from Game.OnRenderIface handling.
Stopped field lifecycle
The draw method clears resources and sets the exported field after the stop check.
Poll VideoPlayback.Stopped only after continuing to draw the instance; the flag becomes true when DrawVideoPlayback observes that the clip stopped.
Ogg video resource
OGV is the stock raw-copy convention; the decoder reads Ogg pages and feeds Theora headers and packets rather than dispatching a generic media framework.
Deliver an Ogg resource containing a Theora video stream through a client-visible RawCopy pack and pass its exact resource path to the video API.
Theora elementary video in Ogg
The bundled path links libtheora directly and has no alternate codec dispatch.
Use a decodable Theora stream with valid dimensions, frame-rate metadata, and one of the supported 4:2:0, 4:2:2, or 4:4:4 pixel formats.
Late fullscreen draw
MainLoop calls ProcessVideo after OnRenderIface, and DrawTexture without source/target regions fills the target.
Expect the built-in frame to draw after Game.OnRenderIface and stretch over the complete current render target without alpha blending.
Queue while active
The enqueue branch is conditional on _video, and ProcessVideo starts queued entries sequentially.
Set enqueue only to append behind an already active fullscreen clip; with no active clip, the request starts immediately and clears any stale queue.
Input interruption
ProcessInputEvent stops the clip before normal input handling for the enumerated event classes.
When canInterrupt is true, key-down, mouse-down, and touch input events stop the active clip; design project skip policy around this broad input set.
Missing fullscreen resource
The void PlayVideo path returns when ReadFile fails and exposes no failure result.
Validate fullscreen resource existence before transitions; a missing file silently leaves no active clip after current playback and queue were cleared.
Separate music pairing
PlayVideo splits the request, loads the first component, and uses only names[1] for SoundManager music.
Use video-path|music-path to stop current music and start a separate one-shot music resource alongside the video; additional separators are not a playlist.
Completion stops music
ProcessVideo unconditionally calls StopMusic when the active clip reports stopped.
Expect fullscreen clip completion or interruption to stop the client's current music group, including music not started by the video.
Fullscreen playback entry point
The exported client method delegates to ClientEngine.PlayVideo.
Use Game.PlayVideo(videoName, canInterrupt, enqueue) for the built-in fullscreen path.
Replacement clears current queue
PlayVideo resets _video and clears _videoQueue before resource lookup.
A non-enqueued request replaces the active clip and clears every queued request before attempting to load the new path.
Playing status includes queued work
ClientEngine reports true for an active playback or a non-empty queue.
Interpret Game.IsVideoPlaying as active-or-queued state, not proof that a frame is currently visible.

entries.source: The current CPU-decoded Ogg/Theora path is revision-pinned while focused native fixtures, production cinematic evidence, and a versioned compatibility policy are missing.
Looping requires explicit proof
SetLooped is exposed through creation, but the current source has no focused loop fixture.
Do not promise looping cinematics until a multi-cycle visible regression proves decoder rewind and frame continuity for the exact asset.
Missing native video fixture
The current native test inventory contains no focused video decoder/playback source.
Treat the lack of Test_*Video* or Test_*Theora* as a coverage gap and keep visible regression evidence mandatory.
Embedding-project acceptance
The Engine supplies decoder and presentation primitives, not a game cinematic system.
An embedding project owns cinematic triggers, recipients, skip/queue policy, subtitles, localization, aspect fit, audio strategy, save consequences, assets, provenance, budgets, and acceptance tests.
Delivered-byte validation
RawCopy is the only delivery transform and runtime paths are exact.
Bake and inspect the exact client resource path and bytes before runtime playback.
Visible-client requirement
No headless or source-only check proves texture upload and presentation.
Validate first frame, motion, end, skip, queue, resize, and texture cleanup in a visible client on every claimed platform.
